description: Use this when you need a fast read on how target buyers or customers would react before you decide or ship: which of 2 to 6 messages, taglines, email subject lines, headlines, ad copy lines, prices, offers or concepts would make them act, or how one option lands. A panel of simulated respondents from the audience you describe (default 12) answers in seconds: who picked each option and a 0 to 10 score for each, the leader and how clear its lead is, why it leads, what holds the others back, one change to make, and simulated quotes. Pass the options exactly as written. To compare new wording, call it again with the same audience: the same panel answers. Results are simulated and directional: not a survey of real people and not live campaign metrics. When the person asks for real people's reactions, use gather_design_study instead (a study with real participants, GatherHQ sign-in). Do not use it to write or rewrite copy, or for market data, benchmarks or news. For a full research report with 10 to 50 interviews, use gather_report_start (GatherHQ sign-in).

audience.description: Who should react, 10 to 1200 characters: roles, company size, industry and location, or a consumer profile. E.g. "Heads of demand generation at US B2B SaaS companies with 50 to 500 employees".

audience_type.description: b2b for business buyers, b2c for consumers. Leave it out to infer it from the audience.

context.description: Up to 2000 characters on the product, offer, price or channel, e.g. "A webinar invite from a customer research company".

options.description: 1 to 6 options, exactly as written: messages, taglines, subject lines, headlines, prices, offers or concepts. With one, you get how it lands; with 2 to 6, which leads.

question.description: What respondents decide, 8 to 400 characters, e.g. "Which subject line would make you open this email?". Default: which would make them most likely to take the next step.

name: gather_quick_read
title: Quick read from simulated buyers
